topic: 7 strange borders, ending on India's tangled enclaves
hook: Your road in Estonia used to run through Russia, and you could not stop, slow down, or step out of the car.
title: 7 Borders That Make No Sense (India's Is Wildest)
description:
Seven real borders that sound fake: a US town you can only reach through Canada, a German town inside Switzerland, a Spanish town inside France, an Estonian road through Russia, and India's land-inside-land-inside-land enclave. Watch the countdown to find out how Cooch Behar's 162 enclaves were finally swapped with Bangladesh in 2015.

#borders #geography #india
comment_prompt: Which border was the strangest: 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 or 1?

chapters.title: 5. Italy's town on a Swiss lake

scenes.narration: Your road in Estonia used to run through Russia, and you could not stop, slow down, or step out of the car.
scenes.headline: A Road Through Russia

scenes.narration: That road is number two on today's list. Number one is in India, where land sat inside land, inside land, inside another country.
scenes.headline: Number One Is Indian

scenes.narration: Seven borders, each one stranger than the last. All real, all on your map, and two of them changed in recent years.
scenes.headline: 7 Real Borders

scenes.narration: We start with an American town that you can only reach by driving through another country.
scenes.headline: US Town, Canadian Road

scenes.narration: Then a German town packed inside Switzerland, an Italian town on a Swiss lake, and a Spanish town sitting in France.
scenes.headline: Towns In Wrong Countries

scenes.narration: Stay till the end, because the last border has a tiny patch of land that sat inside three other pieces of land.
scenes.headline: Stay For Number One

scenes.narration: Number seven. Point Roberts, Washington. It is part of the United States, but you cannot drive there from the rest of it.
scenes.headline: 7. Point Roberts

scenes.narration: Look at the map near Vancouver. A small hook of land hangs below the Canadian coast, and it belongs to America.
scenes.headline: A Hook Of America

scenes.narration: The cause is one straight line. The border follows the 49th parallel, and that line slices through the tip of a peninsula.
scenes.headline: The 49th Parallel

scenes.narration: The land south of the line became American, even though it hangs off Canada with no road joining it to the United States.
scenes.headline: Cut Off By A Line

scenes.narration: So to drive home to the rest of Washington, you cross into Canada, drive through it, and then cross back into America.
scenes.headline: Two Border Checks

scenes.narration: That is two border crossings for a trip inside your own country, just to run a simple errand.
scenes.headline: A Trip Inside Your Country

scenes.narration: Canadian suburbs sit right beside the town, so the border is a short walk from many homes there.
scenes.headline: Border Next Door

scenes.narration: It is a place where the map and the road disagree. And it is not even the strangest one of its kind.
scenes.headline: Map Versus Road

scenes.narration: Next, a town where the shops take Swiss money, but the town is officially German.
scenes.headline: Swiss Money, German Town

scenes.narration: Number six. Büsingen am Hochrhein. It is a German town, and Swiss land surrounds it on every side.
scenes.headline: 6. Büsingen

scenes.narration: Find it on the map beside the Rhine. A small German patch floats inside Switzerland, with no German road joining it to Germany.
scenes.headline: A German Island

scenes.narration: The town is part of Germany, but it sits inside the Swiss customs area, so shopkeepers there use Swiss francs.
scenes.headline: Swiss Customs Zone

scenes.narration: Its cars even have their own number plate code, BÜS, so a German car there stands out at once.
scenes.headline: A Plate Just For BÜS

scenes.narration: Locals say the odd borders came from old deals between old kingdoms, and nobody tidied them up afterwards.
scenes.headline: Old Deals Stuck

scenes.narration: So here is a town where you can walk to Switzerland in minutes, yet it is still German on paper.
scenes.headline: Minutes To Switzerland

scenes.narration: And the next town is stuck even deeper in the same trap, only with a lake and a casino.
scenes.headline: A Lake And A Casino

scenes.narration: Number five. Campione d'Italia. An Italian town that sits on the shore of Lake Lugano, inside Switzerland.
scenes.headline: 5. Campione d'Italia

scenes.narration: Mountains cut the town off from the rest of Italy, so for ages the easy road in and out was a Swiss one.
scenes.headline: Cut Off By Mountains

scenes.narration: Everyday life leaned on Switzerland. People there used Swiss francs and worked with Swiss shops and services.
scenes.headline: Life On Swiss Terms

scenes.narration: In 2020 that changed, and the town joined the European Union's customs area, with the euro as its money.
scenes.headline: Joined EU Customs

scenes.narration: So an Italian town trapped in Switzerland slowly turned into an EU patch in a country outside the EU.
scenes.headline: An EU Patch

scenes.narration: Now a town that has been stuck for more than three hundred and fifty years, thanks to one old word in a treaty.
scenes.headline: One Word In A Treaty

scenes.narration: Number four. Llívia. A Spanish town that sits fully inside France, just beyond the Pyrenees.
scenes.headline: 4. Llívia

scenes.narration: In 1659, Spain and France signed the Treaty of the Pyrenees, and Spain handed over a list of villages to France.
scenes.headline: Treaty Of 1659

scenes.narration: But Llívia was a town, not a village. So by the wording of the treaty, it stayed Spanish.
scenes.headline: Town, Not Village

scenes.narration: That single word kept Llívia Spanish while French land closed in around it, and it is still Spanish today.
scenes.headline: Still Spanish

scenes.narration: A neutral road links it to Spain. That road counts as French land, yet Spanish traffic is allowed on it.
scenes.headline: The Neutral Road

scenes.narration: If you like strange places like this, subscribe, because we find a new one on the map every day.
scenes.headline: Subscribe For More

scenes.narration: Walk the streets of Llívia and you see Spanish signs, Spanish food, and French mountains right outside the town.
scenes.headline: Spain In France

scenes.narration: Fun fact for map fans: its chemist's shop is one of the oldest in Europe, kept as a museum.
scenes.headline: Old Pharmacy Museum

scenes.narration: That was a mistake of one word. The next one is a mistake of a whole map.
scenes.headline: A Mistake Of A Map

scenes.narration: Number three. The Northwest Angle in Minnesota. It is the only part of the lower United States north of the 49th parallel.
scenes.headline: 3. Northwest Angle

scenes.narration: Look at the top of Minnesota on any map. A little square of land pokes up into Canada like a thumb.
scenes.headline: A Thumb Into Canada

scenes.narration: Old treaty makers drew the line using a map that was wrong about where the Mississippi River started.
scenes.headline: A Map That Was Wrong

scenes.narration: When people later checked the real land, the line already stood, and the Angle stayed on the American side.
scenes.headline: The Line Stayed

scenes.narration: Most of it is water in Lake of the Woods, with forest and islands, and no road joins it to the rest of Minnesota.
scenes.headline: No Road To Minnesota

scenes.narration: You can reach the Angle by boat across the lake, or by road through Canada, and then through a border check.
scenes.headline: Boat Or Canada

scenes.narration: People who live there are fully American, yet they go to the next town by crossing a whole other country.
scenes.headline: American, Through Canada

scenes.narration: A wrong map built that border, and the people there still follow it. But next, a border that is not even wrong.
scenes.headline: A Map Error Stays

scenes.narration: It is a road. You can drive on it, but the land under your wheels belongs to another country.
scenes.headline: Land Under Your Wheels

scenes.narration: That road is back, because we are at number two, and it is the one I opened with.
scenes.headline: Back To The Road

scenes.narration: Number two. The Saatse Boot, in south-east Estonia. A road between two Estonian villages that crossed into Russia.
scenes.headline: 2. Saatse Boot

scenes.narration: On a map the Russian land is shaped like a boot, and the road from Värska to Saatse ran straight across it.
scenes.headline: A Boot Of Russia

scenes.narration: The stretch was roughly a kilometre long. Drivers could pass through, but they could not stop, get out, or even slow down.
scenes.headline: No Stopping

scenes.narration: There was no gate and no passport check for people passing through. Just signs, a road, and Russian land on either side.
scenes.headline: No Gate, No Check

scenes.narration: The land stayed Russian because border treaties between Estonia and Russia were never ratified, so the old lines stayed.
scenes.headline: Treaties Never Ratified

scenes.narration: Locals used it every day to get to work, school, and shops, and for years nobody thought twice about it.
scenes.headline: Daily Commute

scenes.narration: Then, in October 2025, armed Russian personnel were seen on the stretch, and Estonia shut the road.
scenes.headline: Closed In 2025

scenes.narration: The government has now closed those road sections for good, with barriers, fences, and signs where cars once passed.
scenes.headline: Closed For Good

scenes.narration: Locals now take a muddy forest road, and a proper bypass is still being built.
scenes.headline: A Muddy Detour

scenes.narration: So the strangest road in Europe, the last one that ran through Russia, is now just a closed piece of history.
scenes.headline: A Road Made History

scenes.narration: Now for number one. It is in India, it involves a football field of land, and it had people living in no-man's land.
scenes.headline: Now, Number One

scenes.narration: Number one. The Cooch Behar enclaves, between West Bengal and Bangladesh. The most tangled border ever drawn.
scenes.headline: 1. Cooch Behar

scenes.narration: For decades, Indian villages sat inside Bangladesh, and Bangladeshi villages sat inside India. In all, there were 162 such patches.
scenes.headline: 162 Patches

scenes.narration: 111 of them were Indian, inside Bangladesh. 51 were Bangladeshi, inside India. Each was a tiny piece of one country, surrounded by the other.
scenes.headline: 111 Indian, 51 Bangladeshi

scenes.narration: A local story says the Maharaja of Cooch Behar and the ruler of Rangpur once played chess or dice for these lands.
scenes.headline: A Game Of Chess?

scenes.narration: Whatever the cause, the patches stayed. If you lived in one, there was no school, hospital, or electricity from your own country.
scenes.headline: Stuck Without Services

scenes.narration: Walk out of your field and you were abroad, with no visa, no papers, and often no easy way to reach your own country.
scenes.headline: A Field Is Abroad

scenes.narration: And then there is the one that blew people's minds, a patch called Dahala Khagrabari.
scenes.headline: Dahala Khagrabari

scenes.narration: It was Indian land inside a Bangladeshi enclave, inside an Indian enclave, inside Bangladesh. The only one of its kind in the world.
scenes.headline: Land Inside Land Inside Land

scenes.narration: It was tiny, about the size of a football field, and stand in the middle and you were standing in four borders at once.
scenes.headline: A Football Field

scenes.narration: Then, at midnight on 31 July 2015, India and Bangladesh finally swapped these lands in a historic deal.
scenes.headline: Midnight, 31 July 2015

scenes.narration: India received 51 Bangladeshi enclaves, and Bangladesh received 111 Indian ones. Maps were redrawn, and the patchwork vanished.
scenes.headline: Maps Redrawn

scenes.narration: People living there could choose which country they wanted to belong to, and many saw their first proper Indian or Bangladeshi flag.
scenes.headline: People Chose A Country

scenes.narration: So the strangest border of all lived in India, and it ended in our lifetime, with the whole thing settled by a pen.
scenes.headline: Ended By A Pen

scenes.narration: That is the countdown: a US town behind Canada, a German town in Switzerland, an Italian one on a lake, and a Spanish one in France.
scenes.headline: The Full Countdown

scenes.narration: Then a bit of America stuck above America, a road through Russia, and India's land inside land inside land.
scenes.headline: All Real Places

scenes.narration: So remember, your road in Estonia really did run through Russia, and you could not stop.
scenes.headline: Your Road, Russia's Land

scenes.narration: Tomorrow: more places on the map that should not exist.
scenes.headline: Tomorrow: More Maps
